title: Obedience and Salvation
definition: Obedience and Salvation explains that obedience does not purchase salvation but reveals living faith and submission to Christ's lordship.
summary: Obedience and Salvation shows that obedience flows from saving faith without becoming the basis of justification.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is Savior and Lord, and His grace trains His people to obey Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Obedience and salvation belong together, but not as cause and payment. Scripture teaches that obedience does not purchase salvation; it flows from faith in the Savior who saves and commands.

This doctrine protects the free grace of the Gospel while refusing to make discipleship optional. The saved person begins to learn the way of Christ.

Jesus is both Savior and Lord. He rescues sinners by grace and then teaches them to obey all that He commanded.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Some fear obedience will compromise grace, while others use grace to excuse disobedience. Scripture holds together free salvation and serious discipleship without confusing their order.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Obey Christ as a grateful disciple, not as a frightened employee trying to earn wages. When you fail, return to grace quickly, confess sin honestly, and keep following the Lord who saved you.
